summary: REBUILD of M1-S04 against the 2026-09-12 amendment (steps[M1-S04].amendments[0]). The round-1 P0 was decided at the plan, option (b): include_logger is now false, ApplicationLogger is gone from templates[] and from the package, and the alert roster is the active assignees of Tier2_Webhook_Admin resolved at run time. Emitted four classes and four .cls-meta.xml siblings at apiVersion 67.0 - Tier2ChannelHealthSchedulable whose execute() is now a single System.enqueueJob and nothing else, Tier2ChannelHealthQueueable with three aggregate COUNT() queries, a PermissionSetAssignment roster query, the email path and a Severity Warning recipient-gap row, an eleven-method Tier2ChannelHealthTest, plus the verbatim TestDataFactory copy the provenance rule still requires. All four skill checkers exit 0. No refusal, and no blocking prerequisite remains: the class set no longer references metadata this build does not ship.
confidence_rationale: GATES.md Gate D row 3: zero unresolved symbols but no target_org_alias, so the dry-run compile did not run at all and coverage is unmeasured - computed MEDIUM, never self-declared HIGH. Gate B resolved every symbol against a file on disk or the platform namespace; the round-1 unmet-metadata finding is closed by the amendment rather than deferred.

findings.title: Round-1 P0 closed by the amendment, not by this step
findings.detail: include_logger:false removes the ApplicationLogger dependency entirely, so Application_Log__c and Logger_Setting__mdt are no longer prerequisites of this step and the package no longer references metadata the build does not ship. Every log call is System.debug: LoggingLevel.ERROR on the three failure paths, INFO/WARN on the run outcome.
findings.recommendation: None. Recorded so the milestone report can see the P0 was decided rather than deferred.

findings.title: The scheduling user's read access to PermissionSetAssignment is granted by nothing this build ships
findings.detail: resolveRecipients() queries PermissionSetAssignment in API 67.0 user mode. Tier2_Webhook_Admin grants Integration_Failure__c permissions and the Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c field permission, and nothing on PermissionSetAssignment. If the scheduling user cannot read it, the query throws or returns empty and every run degrades to the recipient-gap path - writing a Warning row hourly and alerting nobody.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the scheduling user's access at the M1 gate, alongside the A13 assignment check. No answer, decision or step input names this permission.

findings.title: The recipient-gap row counts toward this job's own thresholds
findings.detail: recordRecipientGap() writes an Integration_Failure__c row of Severity Warning, and the threshold queries count rows with no Severity filter because the step input defines rule 1 as 'Integration_Failure__c rows created in the last hour exceed three'. An org with no active assignee therefore accumulates one self-inflicted row per hour, and after four hours rule 1 fires on the job's own output - though it still cannot alert anyone, which is the condition itself.
findings.recommendation: If the gap rows should be excluded, that is a threshold change to the plan, not a code change here. Adding a Severity filter unasked would be inventing a threshold nobody stated.

findings.title: A hardcoded PermissionSet.Name in SOQL is the shape apex-user-and-permission-checks Anti-Pattern 3 flags
findings.detail: That anti-pattern governs GATING behaviour on an assignment, where a Custom Permission is the proper abstraction. This is roster resolution - 'who holds this' is a question FeatureManagement.checkPermission cannot answer - and the requester bound the query explicitly on 2026-09-12. The name is a @TestVisible constant so a rename is one edit. A security scan will flag the line.
findings.recommendation: Read deploy-order.md section 4 item 1 before accepting or overriding a scanner finding on this line. Separately: whether an assignment made through a Permission Set Group still matches PermissionSet.Name = 'Tier2_Webhook_Admin' is stated by no cited skill and is not asserted; Q19 assigns directly, so the query is right for the org as designed.

findings.title: The Case count still depends on record visibility the permission set does not grant
findings.detail: Unchanged from round 1 and untouched by the amendment. Tier2_Webhook_Admin grants viewAllRecords on Integration_Failure__c but carries no Case objectPermissions row (assumption A14), so successesLastDay returns only Cases the scheduling user can see. An under-count makes rule 2 fire on a healthy channel.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the scheduling user's Case access at the M1 gate; the answers name no Case OWD.

findings.title: A healthy run now leaves no durable record anywhere
findings.detail: With include_logger false, the only durable sink this feature has is Integration_Failure__c, and a healthy run has no failure to write there. Dispatch is visible on CronTrigger and AsyncApexJob; the run's own outcome exists only in the debug log.
findings.recommendation: Set a debug-log trace flag on the scheduling user for the first few runs after deploy. deploy-order.md section 6 carries the verification SOQL for both job tables.

findings.title: inputs.recipients and inputs.alert_recipients now disagree in the plan
findings.detail: amend-step replaces inputs wholesale, so the pre-amendment recipients key survived unchanged and still says the address 'is taken from the deploy-order note rather than hardcoded per environment', while the newer alert_recipients binds the PermissionSetAssignment roster. This rebuild implemented the dated, specific one.
findings.recommendation: A prose-only amendment on inputs.recipients would remove the ambiguity for the next reader. Flagged rather than resolved: the runner does not write plan fields beyond status and runs[].

process_observations.observation: The amendment carried a dated requester answer for every value the round-1 build had to mark UNKNOWN, so this rebuild wrote no placeholder and left no // UNKNOWN: marker anywhere in the package.

Dropping the logger also dissolved the round-1 tension between D11's 'does nothing else' and include_logger:true, so execute() is now a single statement and the ambiguity closed without anyone having to adjudicate it.
Noticed that the feature's log sink and its threshold input are the same object with no discriminator, so the job's own gap row is counted as a delivery failure by its next run.
Noticed that the alert roster now depends on read access to a setup object that no artefact in this build grants, which converts a permissions gap into a silent degradation rather than an error.

inputs.recipients and inputs.alert_recipients both survive in the amended plan and say different things; the dated, specific one was implemented and the disagreement recorded rather than quietly resolved.

Whether a Permission Set Group assignment still produces a PermissionSetAssignment row matching the member permission set's Name is stated by no cited skill, so the roster query is documented as correct for the direct assignment Q19 describes rather than asserted in general.
A security pass would independently judge the hardcoded PermissionSet.Name line and the four unqualified 67.0 queries.
process_observations.followup_reason: because the roster query is deliberately the shape one library anti-pattern flags, and a reviewer should see that judgment made independently of the agent that wrote it.
